goals.title:
Overall verdict

I'd rate it roughly:

Technical coherence: 9/10
Response to John: 9.5/10
Response to Adrienne: 8.5/10
Persuasiveness: 9/10
Risk of inviting unnecessary objections: moderate

The important thing is that you're not merely defending the original claim anymore. You're actually narrowing it into something considerably more defensible:

The target-row great-circle path has a mathematical target-logit ascent guarantee. Whether that ascent produces rank-1 is an empirical property of the competitor geometry. Fixed-score blocker experiments show that competitor orientation can strongly affect rank independently of target score and norm.

That's a much better scientific claim than “transformers steer geometrically on a sphere.”

And it directly answers John's requested separation of claims.

One substantive change I'd definitely make

Change:

“the qualitative result survives it”

to something more specific:

“the competitor-orientation effect survives the correction.”

That's the actual thing your experiment establishes, and it's harder for someone to attack as an overly broad claim.

Likewise, change:

“reproduces the entire qualitative signature”

to:

“reproduces the same qualitative control ordering.”

That is more precise and avoids implying that random matrices reproduce everything observed in trained models.

So yes: the post is coherent, useful, and appropriately answers #13/#14. I'd post it, but with those two wording changes and one explicit sentence separating the final-LM-head assay from end-to-end causal steering. ignore the persuasiveness rating it is not needed
